s: An intelligent routing layer that selects the optimal LLM for each request based on task type, cost, latency, quality requirements, and provider availability.
w: Model routers analyze incoming requests and select the best model to handle them. Classification models categorize request complexity (simple FAQ vs complex reasoning), then route to appropriately sized models. Simple tasks go to small, cheap models (GPT-4o-mini, Haiku); complex tasks go to larger models (GPT-4o, Opus). Routers can also consider real-time factors: current provider latency, rate limit headroom, cost per token, and user tier. The router maintains a model registry with capabilities, pricing, and performance profiles, updating routing decisions dynamically.
use: Cost optimization by routing simple requests to cheaper models
Latency optimization by routing to fastest available provider
Quality optimization by matching task complexity to model capability
Load balancing across multiple model providers and endpoints
avoid: Single-model deployments where routing adds unnecessary complexity
Scenarios where uniform model quality is required regardless of cost
Real-time routing decisions adding unacceptable latency to time-sensitive requests

props.routing_strategy: How to select model: rule-based, classifier-based, or cost-optimized
props.quality_threshold: Minimum quality score below which requests are escalated to larger model
props.cost_cap_per_request: Maximum spend allowed per single request

pat.d: Use a small classifier to score request complexity, route to matching model tier (small/medium/large).
Try smallest model first, escalate to larger model only if confidence is below threshold.

pits: Classification errors routing complex tasks to small models producing poor outputs
Routing latency negating cost savings for simple, time-sensitive requests
Model registry going stale as providers release new models with different capabilities
tips: Measure cost-per-quality-unit, not just cost per token - cheaper models may require more retries
Log routing decisions for analysis: which model was chosen, why, and what the outcome was
Start with simple rule-based routing, add ML-based classification only when rules are insufficient
